topic: Beyond the Fold: Mastering Dimensional Shift Geometry Puzzles
target_audience: High school students and curious learners with a basic grasp of Euclidean geometry.

sections.title: The Ant's Perspective: Understanding 2D vs. 3D
lecture_lines: Meet Alpha, an ant living in a 2D world.
Alpha sees objects only as flat lines.
A sphere passes through Alpha's flat plane.
A point grows into a line, then shrinks.
Dimension shifts reveal parts of a hidden whole.
animations: Fade in a large gray rectangle (#808080) representing Alpha's 2D world.
Create a small orange circle (#FFA500) labeled 'Alpha' on the rectangle.
Draw a red circle (#FF0000); highlight a single segment to show Alpha's limited perception.
Animate a green circle (#00FF00) expanding from a point, then shrinking back.
Display the label '3D Sphere Cross-section' in white (#FFFFFF) near the animation.

sections.title: Shadows of Truth: The Logic of Projection
lecture_lines: Higher dimensions cast shadows onto lower ones.
A rotating cube creates complex 2D shadows.
Shadows reveal shapes from many different angles.
animations: Draw a white wireframe cube [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cube.svg] (#FFFFFF) in a 2D perspective view.
Place a yellow parallelogram (#FFFF00) below it to represent its 2D shadow.
Transform the vertices of the cube [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cube.svg] to simulate rotation, morphing the shadow simultaneously.

sections.title: The Net Puzzle: Unfolding the Third Dimension
lecture_lines: A 3D cube can unfold into a net.
Boxy needs to cross this 3D room.
Unfolding the walls reveals a 2D shortcut.
The shortest path is a straight 2D line.
Folding back creates a clever 3D diagonal.
animations: Draw a gray wireframe cube (#A9A9A9) with labeled points A and B.
Morph the wireframe cube into a flat 2D T-shaped net (#DDA0DD).
Draw a straight green line (#00FF00) between A and B on the net.
Morph the net back into the 3D wireframe cube shape.
Highlight the green path as it folds across the cube's faces.

sections.title: Leaping Higher: The Tesseract Challenge
lecture_lines: A moving point traces a one-dimensional line.
Sliding this line creates a two-dimensional square.
Shifting the square forms a three-dimensional cube.
A cube moving into the fourth dimension forms a Tesseract.
Rotating a Tesseract reveals its complex shifting structure.
animations: Animate a white point (#FFFFFF) moving to form a 1D line.
Move the line to trace out a cyan 2D square (#00FFFF).
Shift the square and connect corners to form a white 3D cube (#FFFFFF).
Create a magenta Tesseract (#FF00FF) by nesting a smaller cube inside.
Animate the Tesseract's vertices shifting to represent a 4D rotation.

sections.title: The Wormhole Shortcut: Solving Dimensional Puzzles
lecture_lines: Shifting dimensions lets us fold space itself.
Folding a ribbon brings distant points together.
Higher dimensions create shortcuts impossible in 2D.
animations: Draw a tan ribbon (#DEB887) with a white cat and gray mouse.
Bend the ribbon into a 'U' shape in the 2D plane.
Fold the ribbon ends together so the cat and mouse touch.
